items.title: Review of Insulation Ageing and Lifecycle Management for Oil‐Immersed Power Equipment: From Conventional Testing Analysis to Artificial Intelligence Method
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Oil‐immersed power equipment is a critical component for energy transmission and secure operation of modern power grids. The ageing of oil–paper insulation under combined electrical, thermal and mechanical stresses directly affects equipment lifetime and system reliability. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the ageing behaviour and full‐lifecycle management technologies of oil–paper insulation in oil‐immersed power equipment. First, the structural characteristics of oil–paper insulation and its microscopic ageing mechanisms under multi‐stress conditions are analysed. Subsequently, lifetime calculation models under electrical, thermal, and electro–thermal–mechanical coupled stresses, together with their recent application progress, are systematically summarised. Ageing condition assessment and remaining useful life prediction methods based on characteristic parameter testing and multiphysics techniques are then reviewed, followed by an overview of recent advances in ageing‐state visualisation and dynamic evolution analysis. Finally, this paper discusses artificial intelligence‐oriented intelligent operation and maintenance (O&M) systems, digital twin (DT) modelling and knowledge graph applications. Based on the review, this paper further discusses future research directions, including lifetime degradation mechanisms and dynamic prediction of oil–paper insulation under extreme operating conditions, collaborative O&M management of equipment clusters, DT‐driven proactive safety protection and full‐lifecycle O&M technologies for environmentally friendly oil‐immersed equipment. This review aims to provide a systematic theoretical basis and technical reference for full‐lifecycle management, risk early warning, and the safe and reliable operation of oil‐immersed power equipment.

items.title: Revolutionizing Food Safety through Intelligent Packaging: A Synergistic Approach with AI and Nanotechnology
items.abstract: Despite being a vital component of public health, food safety testing and regulation are difficult, time consuming, and resource intensive. The conventional food safety paradigm is being altered by the incorporation of Food Safety 4.0 technologies, which include deep learning, the Internet of Things (IoT), smartphones, QR codes, and smart packaging, in order to address these issues. The creation of intelligent biosensors that provide real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and improved traceability is essential to this shift, giving regulators and consumers more control over risk management. Intelligent and environmentally friendly packaging is being driven by developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and nanotechnology. While embedded nanosensors identify contamination, spoiling, and changes in the environment, materials like graphene oxide and nanocellulose improve the mechanical and barrier qualities of packaging. AI is important for boosting performance, increasing shelf-life, and increasing the properties of materials by analyzing large datasets. Technologies such as radio frequency identification and computer vision make it possible to track the supply chain and conduct quality control automatically. The emergence of smart packaging technologies such as I2Pack and IMedBox provides an example of how healthcare and food packaging may work together. These systems have features including wireless connections for real-time communication and monitoring, wearable biomedical sensors, and controlled delamination materials. Intelligent packaging has the potential to drastically change how customers interact with products, how safe food is, and how long it lasts. To increase its use in food and pharmaceutical industries in the future, problems with cost, durability, rules, and building customer trust will need to be fixed. But AI, IoT, and nanotechnology together could make food systems more environmentally friendly, smart, and safe.

items.title: RGraph-Eval: Task-Grounded Scene Graphs for Evaluating Robot Video Generation
items.abstract: Generated robot videos can look convincing while depicting the wrong interac- tion: a different object is moved, a grasp disappears, or a placement ends out- side its destination. We introduce RGraph-Eval, a reference-based framework that makes these discrepancies explicit through task-grounded temporal scene graphs. Unlike approaches that construct separate evidence representations for different evaluation dimensions, we organize task entities, interactions, and motion within a unified, interpretable scene graph representation. A foundation-model pipeline identifies manipulation roles, grounds persistent object masks, infers and verifies state transitions and action intervals, and reconstructs manipulated- object motion in three dimensions. Applying this representation to a generated video and a reference demonstration supports an interpretable RGraph-Eval score with visible-object, relation-change, and 3D path-shape components. We also introduce ShareRobot-SG, a collection of 1,000 manipulation scenes from ten ShareRobot sources annotated with the multimodal representation. Our eval- uation separates graph-generation quality from agreement with human video judgments, and includes comparisons with adapted SVG2 and SG-Ego, a bench- mark of three video generators. The framework connects robot-video assessment to the observable entities and interactions underlying a task, while making the graph annotations reusable beyond evaluation. Code will be publicly available at https://github.com/SashaDance/rgraph-eval.

items.title: Robotic Process Automation in Service-Oriented Supply Chains
items.abstract: This chapter examines Robotic Process Automation (RPA) as a digital automation capability for service-oriented supply chains. It explains how software robots automate structured, repetitive, and rule-based tasks across heterogeneous systems, making RPA particularly relevant to service contexts involving order processing, service scheduling, warranty claims, invoice reconciliation, logistics tracking, and customer support. The chapter further clarifies the relationship between RPA and artificial intelligence, arguing that AI acts as an assistive input layer through natural language processing, machine learning, OCR, predictive analytics, and process mining, while RPA remains the primary execution mechanism. Drawing on prior literature and industry examples from logistics, telecommunications, field service, insurance, and product-service systems, the chapter shows that RPA can improve processing speed, accuracy, service consistency, scalability, and employee task reallocation.

items.abstract: The article examines the role of the teacher in developing students’ ability to learn mathematics after the first stage of education within a constructivist framework. Learning to learn is conceptualized as a gradual transition from dependence on the teacher to self-regulation, from supported to independent activity, and from method-oriented instruction to knowledge-centered learning. This process involves cognitive development and the shaping of reflective, conscious participation, in line with the concept of the zone of proximal development, where teacher support is progressively reduced in favour of students’ autonomy. The study was conducted as action research involving 56 fourth-grade students from a public primary school. Iterative instructional interventions enabled examination of the significance of teaching strategies and the organization of the learning environment for students’ cognitive engagement and participation in mathematical activity. The research methods included observation, analysis of students’ work, and unstructured interviews. The teacher is presented as a mediator of meanings, organizer of the learning environment, tutor, and facilitator. The findings highlight the importance of concrete representations, psychological safety, and teacher–student relationships in supporting motivation and students’ learning skills.

items.abstract: Running Persistent AI Worlds (second edition, October 2026) is a review of multi-agent simulations with progressive learning and emergent behaviour: the science of never-ending learning, landmark experiments re-checked, foundation-model-driven open-endedness, societies of language-model agents, learned world models, continual learning and loss of plasticity, the 2026 toolkit, and safety, ethics and validity. Every claim from the February 2026 first edition was re-checked against primary sources, and 248 numbered references link to papers, official lab pages, repositories and package indexes. Two runnable reference simulations in Python and NumPy are included and were run on a 2019 laptop without a GPU: two learning agents in a never-ending seasonal forest (Scenario A), and an evolving population sealed in a fixed energy budget for 1,000 years (Scenario B). items.title: SAFAR-Onto: A Halal Tourism Ontology Developed Through Hybrid AI–Human Engineering
items.abstract: Halal tourism is a fast-growing market. However, information about halal services, certifications, and facilities is scattered across many sources. Existing tourism ontologies model general tourism concepts such as destinations, activities, and accommodations, but they do not represent Islamic requirements such as prayer facilities, halal certification, or dietary compliance. Manual ontology development is slow. Large language models (LLMs) can speed up concept extraction and hierarchy proposal, but they cannot decide religious or cultural matters. In this article, we present SAFAR-Onto, an OWL 2 DL ontology for halal tourism. We develop it through a hybrid AI–human process across four phases: knowledge acquisition, conceptualization, formalization, and dual validation. The process adapts METHONTOLOGY and Simple Knowledge Engineering. LLMs assist with concept extraction and dimensional analysis. An Islamic studies validation gate routes culturally sensitive decisions to human experts. We evaluate the ontology with two methods: expert review across five quality dimensions, and the OQuaRE technical metrics. SAFAR-Onto contains 10 main classes, 75 subclasses, 201 object properties, and 200 data properties, built from 67 validated domain concepts. Six experts from tourism management, computer science, and Islamic studies rated the ontology between 4.0 and 4.5 on a five-point Likert scale, with accuracy highest at 4.5. Fourteen of 18 OQuaRE metrics scored Excellent or Very Good. We also report a verified mapping from expert feedback to ontology revisions. The ontology is publicly available at https://w3id.org/def/SAFAROnto under a CC-BY-4.0 license. We hypothesize that the development process can transfer to adjacent culturally specific domains such as Islamic finance and kosher food systems.

items.title: SAFE AND ETHICAL AI-BASED SELF-HEALING MENTORING FOR STUDENTS OF SMP NEGERI 30 MUARO JAMBI
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides opportunities for students to use technology as a tool to support self-reflection and emotional management. However, its use in the context of mental health requires an understanding of safety, ethics, privacy, and technological limitations. This community service program aimed to provide assistance to students in utilizing AI as a self-healing support tool in a safe, ethical, and responsible manner. The program was conducted at SMP Negeri 30 Muaro Jambi and involved 30 students and a school guidance and counseling teacher as a partner. The program employed a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach through four stages: preparation, core implementation, evaluation, and sustainability. The activities included orientation and initial assessment, emotion and stress recognition, overthinking management, self-healing techniques, AI-assisted self-reflection, and education on the ethics and safety of AI use. Participant responses were evaluated among 24 students using a 1–4 scale instrument covering material comprehension, usefulness, delivery, media, comfort, application of knowledge, and interest in future activities. The evaluation results showed an overall mean score of 3.43 out of 4.00, equivalent to 85.74%, which was categorized as very good. The highest score was found in participants' interest in attending similar activities in the future (90.91%), while all evaluation indicators remained in the very good category. The program indicates that practice-based assistance can help students understand AI as a support tool for self-reflection while strengthening their awareness of privacy, safety, ethics, and the limitations of AI in the context of mental health. Program sustainability is directed toward integrating the materials into school guidance and counseling services and continuing support through the school guidance and counseling teacher.

items.title: Secure Multi-Agent Collaboration Using Large Language Models
items.abstract: As Large Language Models have emerged and become increasingly significant, the way to develop smart multi-agent systems has been transformed, enabling them to communicate, collaborate and decision more efficiently. These systems rely on agents working independently which need to effectively and safely coordinate their actions, to maintain reliability in messy realworld environments. However, bringing LLMs into the mix introduces new risks like data leaks, trickery from bad actors, and trust issues. This paper breaks down a full plan for keeping multi-agent teamwork secure when using LLMs. We look at everything from how they are built and the rules they use to communicate to the safety tools used to stop attacks. We also talk about where this is being used now, the hurdles we still face, and where the tech is headed for building secure AI ecosystems

items.title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems for Pharmaceutical Discovery
items.abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping drug discovery by replacing static models with autonomous, self-improving pipelines. These systems combine large language models, generative chemistry, multi-agent reinforcement learning, simulations, and robotic labs to automate hypothesis generation, molecular design, virtual screening, synthesis, and testing. Closed-loop workflows accelerate decisions, improve prediction accuracy, and minimize redundant experiments. Generative agents create diverse, synthesizable molecules, while simulation agents strengthen ADMET and toxicity prediction. Robotic labs enhance reproducibility and reduce manual workload. Challenges remain in ensuring transparency, avoiding hallucinations, coordinating multi-agent tasks, and meeting regulatory expectations. This chapter outlines the architecture, benefits, and governance needs of agentic AI for faster, safer, and cost-effective drug discovery.

items.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare, but evidence on physicians' selfreported use of, and attitudes toward, these tools remains limited in Egypt and the wider Arab region.Methods: A cross-sectional survey of 293 medical professionals in Egypt was conducted in May 2026 using a 47-item bilingual questionnaire covering demographics, AI use patterns, Likert-scale attitudes and concerns, and self-reported clinical impact. Convenience sampling used professional networks and social media; a single-submission link limited duplicate responses. Percentages are reported against each item's valid (non-missing) denominator, stated with each result.Results: Of 293 respondents, 239 (82.7% of valid responses) reported current AI use. ChatGPT was most used (87.4% of users), followed by Gemini (59.8%). Most respondents (88.9%) supported formal AI training, and 72.1% reported personally identifying inaccurate AI output. Mean trust in AI-generated information was 2.93/5 (median 3, IQR 2–4); mean rating for reviewing AI output before clinical use was 4.11/5. Absence of clear AI regulation received the highest mean concern rating (4.17/5). items.title: Sensor-integrated industrial exoskeletons for ergonomic risk reduction: a systematic review of biomechanical outcomes and intelligent control systems
items.abstract: Introduction Industrial exoskeletons with integrated sensors are emerging as a technology for monitoring biomechanical exposure and supporting the prevention of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in industrial environments. Methods This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, retrieving 106 studies published between 2021 and 2026 from the Scopus and Web of Science databases. VOSviewer version 1.6.20 and R‐Studio version 2026.01.2+418 were used for bibliometric and descriptive analyses. The review provides a qualitative synthesis supported by descriptive quantitative reporting of the extracted outcomes. Results The evidence indicated a technological shift from passive devices toward intelligent exoskeletons integrating surface electromyography, inertial measurement units, machine vision, physiological sensors, and artificial intelligence. Individual studies reported maximum reductions of 68.2% in muscle activity, 34% in spinal compression, and up to 60% in muscle fatigue, alongside productivity improvements of up to 59.5%. Machine learning approaches achieved an ROC of 0.985, automated assessment accuracies of 98.5%, and posture estimation with an ICC of 0.967. However, these values were not pooled estimates and varied across study designs, sensor configurations, tasks, and assessment protocols. Discussion The evidence remains constrained by small sample sizes, sensor drift, interoperability limitations, and insufficient long‐term validation in real‐world industrial environments. Sensor‐integrated exoskeletons show potential for ergonomic monitoring and risk reduction, but their effectiveness and industrial generalizability require further validation through standardized, interoperable, and longitudinal field studies.

items.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
items.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

items.title: SGXAI_FHO: Spiking Graph Explainable Artificial Intelligence with Fire Hawk Optimizer-based fusion of infrared and visible images under low-light conditions
items.abstract: The traditional methods for fusing images acquired under low-light conditions, in many cases, are unable to retain sufficient integrity of structural and textural features, resulting in a distorted and degraded ability to detect features within a scene. This paper presents a novel approach to overcome these issues by using Spiking Graph Explainable Artificial Intelligence (SGXAI) with Fire Hawk Optimization (FHO) to effectively fuse infrared and visible image data. This new SGXAI_FHO framework uses a combination of Gaussian smoothing algorithms to reduce image noise, brightness, and contrast enhancement techniques on visible images to improve the image quality perceived by the human eye (the observer), as well as cross-modal attention (CMA) mechanisms to extract complementary features from the two input modalities and to prioritize these features during the fusion process. The results of this experimentation provide compelling evidence of the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed framework, achieving an F1-score of 99.81%, precision of 99.46%, recall of 99.72%, and accuracy of 99.56%. These results demonstrate that the SGXAI_FHO framework will provide a robust, reliable, and interpretable approach for low-light image fusion and detection applications and has substantial potential for real-world applications.

items.title: SHAPING SELF-REGULATED AND METACOGNITIVE LEARNING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LEARNING ANALYTICS
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics are increasingly embedded in educational systems, yet their implications for self-regulated learning (SRL) and metacognitive development remain only partially understood. This study conducts a systematic literature review of 34 empirical and review articles investigating AI-driven learning analytics in formal education settings, focusing on their impact on SRL, motivation, and academic performance. Following PRISMA-aligned procedures, the review identifies studies involving AI-based analytics tools, standardized SRL or metacognitive assessments, and empirical designs with pre–post or comparison data. The results indicate that AI-driven systems such as predictive models, adaptive platforms, chatbots, and generative AI can strengthen core SRL processes, increase motivation and engagement, and improve academic outcomes across diverse subjects and educational levels. However, the review also reveals persistent implementation challenges, including infrastructural limitations, teacher preparedness, privacy and ethical issues, and potential over-reliance on AI that may weaken independent strategic thinking. The article concludes that AI-driven learning analytics can meaningfully support SRL when embedded within coherent pedagogical frameworks and supported by institutional policies, and it outlines directions for future research on mechanisms, equity, and long-term effects.

items.title: Silicon Samples Match the Answers but Not the Respondents
items.abstract: Silicon sampling generates survey respondents by having a large language model (LLM) answer a survey as a person with given demographic attributes, and the resulting synthetic populations are increasingly used in place of human ones. Existing evaluations focus on individual-answer accuracy, per-question answer distributions, and correlations across questions. None of these compares the respondents themselves, so a generator whose respondents have combinations of answers found in no human respondent can still score well if it reproduces every answer distribution. We propose the respondent coverage gap (RCG), which represents each respondent as a point defined by their complete answer profile and measures how far each human respondent is from the nearest generated one, relative to the distance between human samples. On two US social surveys, all six LLMs we evaluate leave human respondents uncovered, and under our main settings, they fall behind a baseline that samples each answer independently from the human marginals. Across the prompting and inference settings we test, every LLM has a higher RCG than a Gaussian copula fitted to the human data.

items.title: Simulation-based education for enhancing interprofessional crisis resource management and technical competency in perioperative crises: An integrative review
items.abstract: Background Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare, high-acuity perioperative emergency requiring coordinated crisis resource management (CRM). Limited clinical exposure has made simulation-based education central to developing and sustaining CRM competency among perioperative teams. Methods An integrative review guided by the Whittemore and Knafl framework and PRISMA standards searched EMBASE, Scopus, CINAHL, and MEDLINE (October 2025-March 2026). Twenty-seven peer-reviewed publications examining simulation-based CRM and MH management in interprofessional perioperative teams met inclusion criteria. Results Simulation outperformed non-simulation modalities in developing technical and nontechnical skills and team coordination. Structured debriefing drove learning and skills transfer more than active participation. Skills decayed within months without reinforcement but were mitigated by longitudinal and just-in-time training. Cognitive load and human factors frameworks explained performance breakdown and persistent knowledge gaps, and inconsistent readiness emerged as an ongoing patient concern. Conclusion Simulation-based education coupled with structured debriefing and longitudinal reinforcement builds and sustains CRM competency for MH and other perioperative crises. Continuous investment in recurring training, competency assessment, and institutional readiness is needed to translate competence into effective team performance and improved patient outcomes.

items.title: Skin Parameter Scoring Using Artificial Intelligence: A Case Series
items.abstract: Evaluation of facial skin parameters is important for accurate diagnosis and computerized systems can reduce subjectivity. We evaluated the feasibility of an application-based facial analysis artificial intelligence (AI) system by comparing its output to a human dermatologist evaluator. Both an application-based AI and human dermatologist assessed the severity of 14 parameters (age spots, eye bags, moisture, oiliness, redness, texture, wrinkles, acne, droopy lower eyelid, droopy upper eyelid, firmness, dark circles, radiance, pores). The AI generated a raw score between 0 and 100 (100 = flawless) that was converted to match the human rating between 0 and 4 (4 = very severe). Differences in ratings were calculated to determine the degree of agreement. A 0-point difference is defined as complete agreement, a 1-point difference is good, a 2-point difference is poor, a 3-point difference is very poor, and a 4-point difference is worst. In total, 46 facial clinical photos (13 male, 33 female) taken indoors under fluorescent lighting with and without flash were assessed. Parameters with high rates (> 90%) of complete or good agreement were redness (100%), eye bags (96%), and wrinkles (96%). Parameters with moderate rates (80–90%) of agreement were radiance (89%), dark circles (84%), droopy lower eyelid (82%), oiliness (80%), acne (80%), and pores (80%). Parameters with low rates (< 80%) of agreement were texture (78%), age spots (78%), droopy upper eyelid (77%), moisture (72%), and firmness (65%). In a preliminary study of one neural-network AI, its evaluation of skin parameters had an 83% overall complete or good agreement with a human rater. While software-based AI facial analysis systems may lack hardware optimization, they are simple to use and convenient to implement on a variety of hand-held devices. Low start-up costs, rapid data collection, and easy use can be advantages over higher cost, desktop-based facial analysis devices.

items.title: Smart Cold Chains for Perishable Foods: Sensor Fusion, Artificial Intelligence and Dynamic Shelf-Life Management
items.abstract: Food cold chains are increasingly instrumented with connected temperature sensors, intelligent packaging, product-quality measurements and predictive algorithms. Yet the transition from monitoring refrigeration conditions to managing actual product deterioration is neither automatic nor equally reliable across commodities. This critical narrative review evaluates how sensing, multimodal data fusion, artificial intelligence and remaining shelf-life models can support decisions throughout refrigerated food supply chains. Peer-reviewed work published from 2000 to 12 August 2026 was considered, alongside selected foundational studies, through accessible scholarly indexes, bibliographic verification and backward citation examination. Evidence was assessed for biological relevance, measurement validity, independent validation, operational deployment and decision-level consequences. Temperature histories provide an essential but incomplete representation of product condition: packaging atmosphere, initial microbiological or physiological state, humidity, mechanical injury and spatial thermal gradients can materially affect deterioration. Laboratory studies demonstrate promising performance for electronic noses, spectroscopy, flexible indicators and machine-learning models, whereas external route-level validation and calibration across product lots remain comparatively limited. Kinetic models offer interpretable relationships between exposure and quality loss but depend on commodity-specific parameters and assumptions; data-driven models can represent complex patterns but are vulnerable to distribution shift and leakage between training and test samples. Digital-twin and remaining-life allocation studies establish plausible pathways towards first-expired-first-out distribution, yet simulated reductions in waste should not be mistaken for demonstrated commercial benefits. A central distinction is made between marketable quality and microbiological safety: freshness estimates cannot independently establish pathogen absence, extend legally defined use-by dates or replace food-safety controls. The review proposes an uncertainty-aware sequence linking measurement, state estimation, validated remaining-life prediction and constrained operational action. Research priorities include prospective multi-site studies, robust ground truth, calibration transfer, human–algorithm decision trials and transparent accounting of energy, waste and equity. Smart cold chains are best understood as governed decision systems rather than collections of sensors or predictive models.

items.abstract: Online learning platforms provide access to educational content, but many systems deliver the same material to every learner andoffer limited support for identifying individual learning needs. This paper proposes a Smart E-Learning Platform using ArtificialIntelligence (AI) that aims to personalize learning through learner profiles, progress tracking, recommendation methods,automated practice feedback, and a dashboard for learners and instructors. The proposed workflow collects learning activity andassessment results, processes relevant learning indicators, and recommends suitable resources or practice activities. Possible AImethods include rule-based recommendation as a baseline, content-based filtering, and supervised models when sufficientlabelled data is available. The platform is designed as an academic prototype and should be evaluated using measurableindicators such as recommendation relevance, task completion, learner satisfaction, and usability. No implementation results orimprovement percentages are claimed in this proposal. Privacy, transparency, accessibility, and instructor oversight areimportant requirements. The system is intended to support teaching and learning, not to replace teachers or make high-stakesdecisions about students

items.title: Smart Irrigation Systems Fueled by Nano-IoT Integration
items.abstract: Global climate change has affected different factors of society, including agriculture, which is one of the key income factors for a country’s economy. Reports predicting the increase in the human population by 2050 have alerted us to the increase in demand in food production required to support this population. This demand can be achieved before 2050 by a hybrid of traditional agricultural practices blended with technology for sustainable agriculture, soil moisture, plant health, pest control, water management, etc. As water scarcity in some regions has risen due to climate change, efficient water management is critical. These systems combine artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automation with precise real-time sensing. This chapter highlights the value and implications of smart irrigation for effective and sustainable farming methods, which is fueled by nanosensors and Internet of Things technologies. Because they track pH and moisture levels and help with nutrient availability, nanosensors are essential to smart irrigation, allowing farmers to apply fertilizer and water more effectively. items.title: Smart Security and Access Control Systems in Residential Interior Design Projects: A Case Study Approach
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and digital automation technologies have transformed residential environments from conventional living spaces into intelligent ecosystems capable of responding to users’ safety, comfort, and lifestyle requirements. Traditionally, residential security systems were primarily dependent on mechanical locks, physical surveillance, and human monitoring. However, contemporary smart security systems integrate biometric authentication, intelligent surveillance, automated access control, sensor-based monitoring, and cloud-connected platforms to create responsive and adaptive residential environments. This review paper explores the integration of smart security and access control systems within residential interior design projects through a case study approach. The study examines how technological interventions influence spatial planning, material selection, user interaction, and aesthetic considerations in modern residential interiors. A qualitative review methodology is adopted by analysing existing research, technological frameworks, and representative residential applications. The paper evaluates major components including smart locks, biometric systems, video doorbells, motion sensors, AI-enabled cameras, integrated home automation platforms, and cybersecurity mechanisms. The study proposes an integrated design framework demonstrating how security technologies can be embedded within residential interiors without compromising visual quality and spatial experience. The findings indicate that successful implementation requires collaboration between interior designers, architects, technology consultants, and homeowners during early design stages. The paper highlights that future residential interior will increasingly depend on invisible, intelligent, and user-centred security systems where safety becomes an integrated design feature rather than an independent technological addition.

items.title: Social-HUMINT: An LLM-Augmented Unified Framework for Measuring Social Media Exposure
items.abstract: In the post-API landscape, social-media profiling has become inexpensive and automated: Large Language Models (LLMs) can extract structured information from unstructured content and deduce attributes users never disclosed. A person's true exposure is not what they post but what can be inferred from it. As these practices become routine, exposure to social engineering attacks becomes an operational certainty, demanding a shared framework for assessment and mitigation. We make this exposure measurable by quantifying how accurately a target can be profiled, and how far that profile enables social engineering attacks. Because no existing model fully spans this continuum, we unify Social Media Intelligence (SOCMINT) and Cyber Human Intelligence (Cyber-HUMINT), two individual-focused disciplines that evolved separately, into a single doctrine-grounded taxonomy of 38 capabilities across the Cyber Threat Intelligence lifecycle, where user profiling bridges passive collection and active engagement. Domain experts validated the taxonomy (Fleiss' $κ$ = 0.92). We operationalize its core path (extraction, inference, and susceptibility assessment) as an LLM-augmented multi-agent pipeline, evaluated on real participants' public data. Susceptibility is assessed indirectly: the pipeline predicts how each target would rank personalized engagement options, matching their actual choices significantly above chance. This ranking capacity captures the personalization on which tailored attacks depend. The underlying profiles are accurate: extraction reaches F1 = 97.3%, and inferred attributes score 4.73/5, both far above rule-based and NER-based baselines at negligible cost. The framework augments security analysts' tradecraft rather than replacing it and enables defenders to gauge their own exposure before an adversary does.

items.title: Sociological_and_Psychological_Implications_of_AI_Infofagia
items.abstract: The advent and rapid spread of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative Artificial Intelligencesystems have marked an epistemological and structural discontinuity in the Information Society.While the early phases of the digital transition were characterized by processes of digitization, indexing,and heuristic data retrieval — where the machine acted primarily as an archivist or intermediary towardprimary content —, the current configuration of algorithmic architecture responds to a qualitativelydifferent dynamic. Artificial Intelligence does not merely organize human knowledge; to function,learn its semantic structures, and provide real-time synthesis, it requires the continuous, massive, andsystematic assimilation of informational material produced by humanity.To describe this phenomenon of insatiable and structural nourishment, we propose here the analyticalcategory of «infofagia» (derived from the Greek root phagêin, "to eat", combined with the informationalprefix). AI infofagia does not constitute a mere computational phase of the machine — the technicalphase of training on datasets —, but rather a total sociological and psychological fact. It identifies anextractive and metabolic process in which humanity's entire cultural, scientific, artistic, andconversational production is converted into raw matter, "ingested" by mathematical models, digested,and finally returned in the form of synthetic and normalized output.Adopting the paradigm of infofagia allows us to overcome both purely deterministic readings oftechnology and apologetic visions tied to the alleged democratization of knowledge. Through theanalysis of empirical data, international case studies, and clinical-social feedback, this essaydemonstrates how the informational appetite of large algorithmic models is not neutral, but directlyretroacts upon economic structures, cultural diversity, and the psyche of the final consumer.

items.title: Sovereign AI in the Developing Global South: Architecting Strategic Autonomy in the Intelligence Economy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is turning the older digital divide of the developing world into an intelligence-economy participation divide: an asymmetry in the capacity of states to shape, own, govern and draw value from cognitive automation. Read against the literatures on digital colonialism, data extractivism and the "Data Nullius" framework, this article treats Sovereign AI as a distinct policy object for the Global South rather than a subset of digital public infrastructure or industrial policy. It sets out four interlocking registers of sovereignty (compute, supply chain, model and data) and argues for a modular, developmental architecture governed through "fluid institutionalism", built on the principle of foundations before the frontier: connectivity, device affordability and FAIR-aligned digital public infrastructure first, then retrieval-grounded small language models. The article then examines whole-of-government interoperability and tiered human-in-the-loop governance; economic transformation through public procurement; security resilience through inbound and outbound data embassies; local-language models such as Bhashini and InkubaLM; a "choose partners, not sides" posture in a bipolar technology rivalry; and South-South cooperation for a stronger voice in global AI governance. It closes with the binding constraints of energy, water, fiscal capacity and coordination, an assessment of risks including dependency lock-in, elite capture and linguistic exclusion, and a time-phased set of recommendations by institutional actor.

items.title: Sovereign AI in the Developing Global South: Volume III – Conflicts, Insurgencies, and Algorithmic Warcraft vs. Statecraft
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is collapsing the historical separation between statecraft and warcraft. This third volume of the series on Sovereign AI in the developing Global South examines how algorithmic systems are restructuring state authority in domestic governance and armed conflict. It first analyses "algorithmic statecraft": biometric digital public infrastructure and the risk of function creep, with India's Aadhaar and Kenya's Huduma Namba as cases, and predictive policing as a form of actuarial justice that can codify structural discrimination. The article then turns to "algorithmic warcraft": AI decision support systems used for target generation in Gaza, automation bias and the "triage trap" that hollow out meaningful human control, and bias in military AI. It traces the democratisation of lethality through commercial and AI-enabled drones in Myanmar, Sudan, Libya and the Sahel, Bangladesh's border-security modernisation in response to regional spillover, and generative AI as an instrument of cognitive warfare. It closes with the fractured diplomacy of the Global South in the UN Group of Governmental Experts on lethal autonomous weapons systems, and argues that sovereign resilience requires contextualised AI frameworks under strict civilian oversight together with a coordinated push for binding international norms.

items.title: Spatial-Matrix Attention in Atypical Cognition: Full-Grid Dynamic Scanning and Mid-Sweep Directional Switching as a Model for Next-Generation Non-Linear AI Architectures
items.abstract: Standard large language model (LLM) architectures process natural language sequentially using one-dimensional positional encodings and autoregressive causal masks. While effective for localized sequence generation, this serial pipeline creates severe processing bottlenecks during global structural synthesis, cross-modal translation, and parallel error detection. In contrast, neurodivergent human cognitive processing—specifically visual-spatial dyslexic architectures—treats textual and symbolic input as a two-dimensional spatial coordinate plane. Rather than relying on rigid, single-direction visual paths, this cognitive model deploys simultaneous multi-directional raster sweeps: horizontal (left-to-right, right-to-left), vertical (top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top), diagonal X-pattern scans, and dynamic mid-pass directional pivots upon semantic or structural convergence. This monograph formalizes Spatial-Matrix Attention (SMA), an artificial intelligence attention paradigm that replaces one-dimensional token queues with a 2D Euclidean coordinate tensor. By assigning spatial coordinates to tokens and enabling dynamic vector scanning with early-stopping pointer retrieval, SMA allows machine learning models to execute asynchronous parallel drafting, real-time self-proofreading, and low-latency ontological memory access without requiring heavy autoregressive re-evaluation passes. Main Highlights & Key Contributions: 2D Coordinate Embeddings: Replaces standard 1D sequential indexing with a dynamic 2D Euclidean spatial distance matrix and relative angular orientation tensors. Multi-Vector Matrix Rastering: Formalizes vertical column sweeps, cross-planar diagonal scans, and horizontal parsing for global layout and structural density verification. Mid-Sweep Directional Pivoting: Introduces stochastic angle switching and early stopping during raster passes when key semantic thresholds or structural anomalies are detected. Key-Bound Pointer Retrieval: Enables direct execution of pre-cached ontological macros, drastically reducing KV-cache expansion overhead during long-context reasoning.

items.abstract: This multi-volume monograph series introduces Spatial-Matrix Processing, a non-linear language comprehension framework that bridges human visuospatial cognition and next-generation artificial intelligence architecture. Moving beyond the rigid one-dimensional (1D) serial token processing of traditional autoregressive transformers, this work formalizes how language can be evaluated across a two-dimensional (2D) topological canvas. Inspired by the parallel scanning mechanics observed in visuospatial dyslexia—specifically multi-directional raster sweeps (X-pattern, diagonal, and inverse passes)—the framework demonstrates how semantic derivation can bypass sequential token queues in favor of key-bound spatial pointer retrieval. Volume I (Cognitive Architecture & System Blueprint) establishes the human cognitive foundations, contrasting 1D linear attention bottlenecks with 2D spatial-grid parsing. It outlines the architectural design for Spatial-Grid Attention (SGA) and real-time parallel compiling (simultaneous drafting and proofreading). Volume II (Mathematical & Thermodynamic Foundations) provides standalone mathematical rigor, deriving field-theoretic semantic emergence equations, pointer address collision probabilities (P_addr), dynamic resolution throttling algorithms (2D Spatial <-> 1D Linear fallback), and topological conservation under orthographic transposition. It presents the Zero-Entropy Error Transmutation Lemma, proving how structural disorder (such as letter transpositions) can be absorbed and transmuted into high-fidelity semantic intent without information loss.

items.title: Spectral Smoothing and Spiking Perturbations Reconfigure Capability Profiles and Selective Task Performance in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Singular-value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed-forward projections, yet their causal role in downstream behavior remains underexplored. We study post-hoc spectral smoothing and spiking interventions on the up_proj and down_proj matrices. Positive perturbation stretches deviations from the geometric mean, making large singular values larger and small ones smaller (spiking), and vice versa. The intervention preserves singular vectors and the geometric mean of the singular values. Across five open Llama and Qwen instruction models, we evaluate the perturbed systems on capability-labeled subtasks, standard and chain-of-thought reasoning benchmarks, judge-scored truthfulness, hallucination, and safety tasks, and TRAIT personality probes. To interpret score shifts, we fit responses in a three-dimensional capability basis consisting of factual knowledge, language understanding, and deductive reasoning. The induced changes suggest structured rather than purely random sensitivity: large positive perturbations more reliably suppress language and deductive responses, moderate negative perturbations can sometimes improve factual or task-local performance on the evaluated grids, and sensitivity varies strongly by model family, benchmark module, and underlying layerwise spectral inequality. These results position spectral perturbation as a lightweight intervention for probing how capabilities are organized and traded off in large language models.

items.title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training
items.abstract: Vector quantization (VQ), in particular lattice-based methods, offer strong rate-distortion trade-offs for low-bit large language models (LLMs), yet their behavior under quantization-aware training (VQ-QAT) remains poorly understood. We scale lattice VQ-QAT to billion-parameter LLMs and multi-billion-token training regimes, and introduce SQuAT, a shape-gain VQ-QAT approach trained with a separate straight-through estimator (STE) for the shape and gain. SQuAT decomposes weights into direction and magnitude: normalized directions are quantized using an $E_8$-derived spherical codebook, while gains are quantized independently with low-bit scalar quantizers. We show that, unlike a standard STE applied to the full quantizer, which ignores the shape-gain structure, these separate STEs induce tangent-space updates for directions, yielding an implicit form of spherical (Riemannian) optimization. To enable scalability, we develop a distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme, in which workers quantize disjoint weight blocks and communicate only discrete indices, reducing VQ-QAT training time by 12.8$\times$ and allowing us to scale it to 10B tokens. Across instruction-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B, Qwen3-4B, and base Qwen3-1.7B, SQuAT consistently outperforms standard VQ-QAT STE under identical quantizers and initialization, and achieves SOTA VQ-QAT accuracy.

items.title: Stage aware synthetic generation of high quality human blastocyst images using StyleGAN3 with multi level validation
items.abstract: The lack of large, balanced, and shareable biomedical imaging datasets remains a major barrier to the development, validation, and clinical translation of artificial intelligence systems. Synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising solution, yet its real-world value critically depends on rigorous validation beyond visual realism. In this study, we present and systematically evaluate a stage-aware generative framework based on StyleGAN3 for high-fidelity biomedical image synthesis, using human embryo development in Assisted Reproductive Technology. The StyleGAN3 models are trained to synthesize embryo images at the Start of Blastulation and Blastocyst stages, using a curated cohort of 96 high-quality embryos (selected from an original set of 704 time-lapse IVF videos based on combined ICM/TE Gardner grades of AA, AB, or BA). To assess reliability and practical utility, we introduce a multi-level evaluation protocol integrating distributional similarity (Frechet Inception Distance), frequency-domain spectral analysis, and downstream task-based validation. Experimental results show that the proposed models accurately reproduce global morphological characteristics, with consistently higher fidelity and stability at earlier developmental stages (FID = 52.1), while later-stage synthesis is challenged by intrinsic data imbalance and heterogeneity. items.title: Students’ Engagement in Extensive Reading Activities in English at University of Mataram
items.abstract: This study investigated students’ engagement in Extensive Reading activities among English Education students at the University of Mataram. It aimed to describe students’ behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement and to identify the factors influencing their engagement. Although previous studies have reported the benefits of Extensive Reading for language proficiency and motivation, relatively little research has simultaneously examined the three engagement dimensions and their contextual influences in Indonesian EFL higher education. A qualitative descriptive design was employed with ten students completing a questionnaire and five students participating in semi-structured interviews. The closed-ended questionnaire functioned only as descriptive supporting data, while the semi-structured interviews provided the main qualitative explanations; therefore, the study was not designed as mixed methods and did not use inferential statistics. The questionnaire was used to identify general patterns through descriptive frequencies and percentages, while the interviews provided more detailed explanations of students’ reading experiences. The findings showed generally positive engagement. Behavioral engagement was reflected in relatively strong participation and effort, although reading consistency remained the main challenge. Emotional engagement was shown through interest, enjoyment, motivation, and positive attitudes toward English reading. Cognitive engagement appeared through reading strategies, comprehension monitoring, reflection, and connections between texts and prior knowledge. Five factors influenced engagement: reading materials and personal interest, language difficulty, time and academic responsibilities, motivation and academic requirements, and reading autonomy and lecturer support. Overall, students’ engagement in Extensive Reading was shaped by interacting personal, textual, and academic conditions.

items.title: STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS ON AI TRANSLATION: A THEMATIC ANALYSIS
items.abstract: In addition to the availability of machine translation technologies such as Google Translate, people now have the option of employing Generative AI to carry out the translation tasks. GenAI is capable of producing translations in any language in a quick and efficient manner. Students in English department who might be interested in pursuing careers as language translators in the future, should have mastered artificial intelligence technologies in order to thrive in the world that is always changing. The purpose of this study is to investigate the students’ perceptions regarding the employment of artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT for translating texts. This study was presented with two research questions, which are as follows: To what extent do students position AI translation tools in relation to human translation? When it comes to the employment of artificial intelligence for translation, what benefits and concerns shapes students’ attitude toward AI translation use? In order to collect the necessary information for this study, interviews were conducted with twenty-two students from English department at Binus University who were enrolled in Translation course. The interview transcripts were used as the data for this study, and they were analysed qualitatively using thematic analysis framework developed by Braun and Clarke (2006). There are three fundamental steps involved in doing thematic analysis. Starting with initial open coding, which involves classifying data into codes. The second step is grouping the similar codes and finally, defining and naming the themes for each group. Results show that five themes appear in this analysis. These are: conditional acceptance of AI translation, perceived advantages of AI translation, concerns about overdependence, human superiority in meaning, and ethical and institutional boundaries. The findings suggest that even though artificial intelligence translation is effective, it is still a limited tool that must continue to be controlled by humans.

items.title: Survey on intelligent video surveillance
items.abstract: Abstract Video surveillance systems have witnessed rapid advancements over the past two decades, fueled by progress in computer vision, artificial intelligence, and edge computing. However, despite extensive research, there remains a need for a review that synthesizes the architectures, methodologies, and evolving trends of intelligent video surveillance systems from a system-level perspective. Most existing literature reviews focus narrowly on individual tasks such as object detection, motion tracking, or anomaly recognition, without addressing how these components integrate within a complete system. This paper addresses this gap by conducting a systematic review of research published between January 2000 and July 2025, drawing from major digital repositories. The main contributions of this work are threefold: (1) it proposes a structured taxonomy of intelligent surveillance systems based on key functionalities, including object detection, motion tracking, abnormal event detection, vehicle and traffic monitoring, object counting, and multi-camera coordination; (2) it provides a comparative analysis of methodologies, datasets, and platforms used across studies; and (3) it explores the interconnections among these core tasks while identifying critical challenges such as real-time processing, privacy preservation, data scalability, and system interoperability. Key outcomes of this review include the identification of underexplored research areas—such as federated learning and cross-camera integration—and practical guidelines for designing next-generation surveillance systems. The literature analyzed was sourced from major digital repositories including IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, arXiv, Springer, and the ACM Digital Library.

items.title: Sustainability Aspects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education: A Law and Economics Analysis
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming human societies. In the many attempts to capture the novel trend of AI entering in all aspects of human life these days, hardly any research covers sustainability aspects of AI encroaching society. In the teaching of sustainability, AI appears as an way to improve carbon footprint as for energy savings opportunities – for instance by using online resources instead of physical books, reducing cognitive load of tedious tasks that had to be performed in educational settings previously, such as sifting through many books to find applicable cases in law school etc. At the same time, AI may create enormous environmental costs – e.g., through its electricity consumption use for big data storage and analytics – but also sustainability challenges – e.g., through eternally-living algorithms and technical devices. This chapter proposes weighing the costs and benefits of AI in sustainability education. In a Law & Economics analysis, the advantages and disadvantages of AI in sustainability education will be compared in order to present a framework to harvest the benefits but prepare for coping with the downsides of AI in sustainability education. Future student learning experience enhancement and educational changes due to AI in the future will be prospectively anticipated in the discussion. The future of education may positively develop in less cognitive load and diligent learning-by-heart but shift towards creative solution finding, navigating through a digital online jungle and development social network skills to find the right tools in a growing ocean of mushrooming AI advancements.

items.abstract: The development of digital technology, artificial intelligence, environmental concerns, and changing workforce needs has encouraged organizations to adopt more sustainable approaches to talent management. This study aims to examine the development of sustainable talent management, identify its key practices, and analyze the role of digitalization, artificial intelligence, employee skill development, motivation, and retention in supporting organizational sustainability. This study employs a qualitative approach using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Relevant studies were identified through systematic searches of selected databases, screened according to predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed using content analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that sustainable talent management has evolved from a short-term, performance-oriented approach toward a more strategic and long-term perspective that emphasizes organizational sustainability and employee development. Its key practices include talent attraction and selection, competency development, employee motivation, and retention, supported by digital technologies and artificial intelligence. However, the implementation of these technologies requires continuous employee skill development and a human-centered approach to ensure that technological advancement remains aligned with employee and organizational needs. The study concludes that sustainable talent management integrates technological, human, social, and environmental aspects to support organizational sustainability and long-term organizational resilience.

items.title: Synthesis of Reliable Logic Question Answering Data for Large Language Model with Aid of Operations Research Program
items.abstract: Logical reasoning is a highly valued capability in language models. However, high-quality logical reasoning data remain scarce, while manual data creation is costly and time-consuming. We introduce Operations Research Aided Synthesis (ORAS), a solver-verified, two-layer incremental framework for synthesizing logic question-answering data. ORAS leverages operations research techniques to systematically generate high-quality datasets for evaluating large language models (LLMs) and, when used for training, improving their reasoning capabilities. ORAS's pipeline integrates mathematical programming methods to generate question-answer pairs, and then employs a dual-phase approach: the first phase uses optimization algorithms to construct and evaluate the logic systems by solving the problem using a mathematical solver. The second phase translates the logic system to human-readable problems and generates answers according to the information from the mathematical solver. The fine-tuned model achieves a 22%-33% (percentage point) improvement in accuracy on in-sample tests and a 4%-22% (percentage point) improvement on similar out-of-sample tests.

items.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
items.abstract: Nepali-English code-switched conversational speech presents severe challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR), chiefly through script confusion (inappropriate mixing of Devanagari and Latin orthography) and elevated error rates at language switch points. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can adapt multilingual foundation models, but human code-switched audio is expensive to collect and annotate. We curate a new benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total; 10,214 test, 2,830 dev), audited and verified to eliminate machine translation leakages and acoustic loops. We investigate a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework: Stage 1 applies SFT on 0.95 h of speech synthesized via a multi-speaker, dual-engine TTS pipeline; Stage 2 explores Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with transcription and script rewards. We find that synthetic SFT provides the primary cross-domain transfer to spontaneous human speech, reducing Mixed Error Rate (MER) from 23.40% to 21.52% (-1.88 pp) and switch-point error rate (SPER) from 35.89% to 28.77% (-7.12 pp). Subsequent GRPO yields small, statistically significant adjustments on 173 test utterances (1.69%), driving English script confusion (SCR_en) from 6.45% to 6.36% (p <= 0.001) and SPER to 28.70% (p = 0.022 clustered). Crucially, ablation reveals that in this SFT-converged encoder-decoder setting, an auxiliary script reward term yields performance identical to MER-only optimization because rollout candidate groups exhibit near-zero script variance on synthetic data. On monolingual benchmarks, SFT improves Nepali MER by 2.71 pp (stabilizing at 18.42% after GRPO, a 2.38 pp gain over baseline) while preserving English lexical WER (3.38% vs. 3.33%). Verified transcripts, timestamps, episode metadata, and reconstruction scripts are publicly released.

items.title: SyRA-CS: Synthetic-to-Real Adaptation for Code-Switched ASR with Meta-Learning
items.abstract: Code-switched (CS) automatic speech recognition (ASR) remains difficult because real CS speech is scarce and synthetic speech does not fully match it. We investigate whether synthetic CS speech is more useful for learning an adaptation-friendly initialization than for ordinary continual fine-tuning. We propose SyRA-CS, a pair-specific synthetic-to-real adaptation framework based on Reptile meta-learning. For each language pair and pretrained model, we meta-train on the corresponding synthetic CS-FLEURS subset and then adapt using one hour of labeled real target speech. We evaluate four architectural settings: Encoder-CTC, FastConformer-RNN-T, Attention Encoder-Decoder (AED) and Speech-LLM. Experiments cover on Arabic-, French-, German-, and Hindi-English, against synthetic-only transfer, real-only fine-tuning, and continual fine-tuning. SyRA-CS improves over continual fine-tuning on WER in all 16 model-pair comparisons and on CER in 15 of 16, with relative macro WER reductions of 17.7% for XLS-R and 5.3-5.8% for the other three models. The gains hold across the tested models but vary in size across architectures, language pairs and metrics.

items.title: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF CURRENT AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES OF ROBOTIC PARTIAL NEPHRECTOMY
items.abstract: Background: Nephron-sparing surgery has become a standard approach for localized renal masses because it preserves renal function while providing oncologic control comparable with radical nephrectomy. Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) has expanded the minimally invasive management of increasingly complex renal tumors. This review summarizes contemporary clinical outcomes and emerging technologies in RAPN. Materials and Methods: A PRISMA-guided literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus for peer-reviewed English-language human studies published between January 2020 and June 2025. Search terms included robot-assisted partial nephrectomy, robotic partial nephrectomy, RAPN, nephron-sparing surgery, single-port robotics, augmented reality, three-dimensional surgical planning, fluorescence-guided nephrectomy, and learning curve. Manual reference screening was also performed. Twenty eligible studies were included for qualitative synthesis; quantitative meta-analysis was not performed because of heterogeneity in study designs and endpoints. Results: Comparative randomized, propensity-matched, and multicenter studies generally showed faster postoperative recovery, less pain, and shorter hospitalization with RAPN than with open partial nephrectomy, while maintaining comparable oncologic outcomes. RAPN was feasible for hilar, endophytic, and solitary-kidney tumors in experienced centers. Three-dimensional planning and augmented-reality guidance improved anatomical visualization and operative planning, while indocyanine-green near-infrared fluorescence supported selective ischemia and perfusion assessment. Single-port RAPN demonstrated broadly comparable perioperative outcomes with multiport approaches, although early adoption may involve longer operative times. Structured learning-curve and training models were associated with progressive improvement in operative performance and complication rates. Conclusion: Current evidence supports RAPN as a safe and effective nephron-sparing approach across a broad range of renal tumor complexity. Artificial intelligence-assisted image guidance, fluorescence-based perfusion assessment, three-dimensional planning, and next-generation single-port platforms may further improve precision and functional preservation. Larger multicenter randomized studies and longer follow-up are needed to establish durable oncologic, functional, and cost-effectiveness benchmarks.
